title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 92
paragraphs: The Lycians furnished fifty ships. They wore corselets and greaves, and carried bows of cornel-wood, featherless reed arrows, javelins, and a goat-skin slung over the shoulder; on their heads they wore feather-wreathed felt caps, and they carried daggers and falchions as well. The Lycians were formerly called Termilae, being originally from Crete, and they took their later name from Lycus son of Pandion, an Athenian.
